## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The PR changes the header check in `parse_report` from a prefix match on `"REPORT "` to an exact match on `"REPORT v1"`, and adds two tests. The production change is correct and has no other callers in the repository. `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` properly covers the new rejection branch. `test_rejects_legacy_header` is misnamed and doesn't test what its comment says.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- tests/test_report.py:8 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` builds `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. `rsplit("v1", 1)` swaps the last `v1`, which is in the body, not the header. The input also has no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at the trailer check in `app/report.py:3`. It never reaches the version check, and the comment at line 9 ("Guards the new version check by changing the fixture's version to v0") is wrong. — The test passes with the old `startswith("REPORT ")` code too, so it can't catch a regression in the header check it is named for. It only looks like extra coverage.

## Strengths
- `app/report.py:5` now requires an exact `"REPORT v1"` header, so `parse_report` rejects unsupported versions such as `REPORT v0` and `REPORT v10`. The old prefix match accepted them.
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` passes a complete, well-formed report with a `v0` header. It fails on the old code and passes on the new code, so it really tests the change.
